findings.reason: the section must name `resolve_shotset_version` and the `SHOTSET_VERSION` guard as the owner to extend (keyed by machine) or the JT-60SA baseline cannot be stamped under its own label or run through the comparability guard.
findings.text: §7 adds "a second named set in that module with its own version label" for the JT-60SA baseline, but `resolve_shotset_version` compares only against the single `FROZEN_SHOTSET` (shots.py:74-77) and returns the single `SHOTSET_VERSION` constant, and `parity.py:537` rejects any stamp whose `shotset_version` is not that one constant; a JT-60SA set therefore resolves to `AD_HOC_SHOTSET_VERSION` and its stamp carries neither its own label nor a passing parity comparison, contradicting §7's done-when that the JT-60SA stamp is labelled by its set and that `resolve_shotset_version` already "compares (machine, shot_id, role)"

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the substantial new behaviour lands behind the modules that already own it: the EQDB request/record/refusal types and the grid record writer extend `imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py` (`RemoteEddbExtractor`, `encode_batch`/`decode_batch`) and `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py` (`write_channel`'s token/overwrite invariants) instead of a parallel store, and the pin table hides machine selection behind the existing `resolve_machine_description` — no family of shallow wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds a second frozen shot set beside MAST's without naming that the resolver and the parity guard that turn a set into its label are single-valued.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 (read 2026-10-06T20:54:42Z); each section that adds public surface names, in its own text, what it retires/merges or why nothing can be, and each such statement checked against the tree: §2 adds one public resolver and retires the exporter's `_cocos_transformation`; §6 adds the EQDB request/record/refusal types and `read_signal_map_observation` (retiring `read_catalogue_observation`) and states it adds no refusal family because a transport fault stays `EddbRemoteError`; §7 retires the three `PINNED_*` constants and their `machine_artifact_arm` re-export behind one machine-keyed table.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and extends the existing owner for every mechanism it adds: the exporter's private COCOS resolver (`imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py:147`) is retired in favour of the transform engine's (`imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:411`); the §6/§7 SELENE chain reuses `build_geometry_from_arrays` (`imas_ambix/worldmodel/equilibrium_labels.py:465`) through the existing `read_efit_geometry(..., loader=)` seam (`imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py:120`) rather than reading SELENE twice; and a grep for `eqdb` across `imas_ambix/` returns nothing, confirming the plan's claim that no equilibrium-database reader exists to reuse.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no proposed layer wraps existing machinery without justification: the SELENE reference loader and the FAME loader are adapters over the typed `EfitLabels` record (`imas_ambix/challenge/loader.py`), and the plan argues each reuse against a parallel path rather than adding one.
